newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends weak on doubts over loss estimates.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends weak on doubts over loss estimates.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter futures settled lower on ideas that initial estimates may have overstated the amount of freeze damage to the HRW wheat crop, traders said.
"You can probably chalk this up to ongoing reductions in estimates of crop damage. Plus, cash basis levels felt weak," a KCBT trader said at the close.

Early estimates of total losses caused by last weekend's freeze in the U.S. Plains ranged from 60 million to 200 million bushels, but traders said it will be several days or even weeks before more accurate estimates emerge.

Traders said pressure at the midsession came from a wire service report saying an Indiana farmer died of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a rare but deadly brain disease said to be the human form of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy, also known as "mad cow disease." The report also said the victim's wife speculated that he may have contracted the disease by using garden fertilizer containing bone meal.

The report sent CME live cattle prices reeling. Grains tumbled on the report initially but then rebounded amid ideas the story could force more restrictive use of animal protein in feed, which would be supportive for grains and soybeans.
KCBT wheat settled two to 7-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 5-1/2 cents at $4.65. New crop July closed down 7-3/4 cents at $4.40.
Traders said Prudential Securities sold 1.3 million July bushels and bought one million July. Linnco (LFG) sold one million July and also bear-spread one million Sept/July bushels at 14 cents.
